text:
alex: Heads up — seeing NVMe temp-gradient spikes on ap-southeast1 GNode fleet. When the gradient > ~18C across drives on the same host the controller enters thermal throttle and IOPS drops ~50-70%, which is causing GPU attach timeouts and provisioning failures.

rachel: dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/NVME/temperature-gradient?orgId=1 (just flagged the cluster view) :chart_with_downwards_trend:

alex: snippet from dmesg on node gnode-ase1-042:
```
[ 1283.412345] nvme nvme0: temperature-sensor delta=22C, controller entering thermal throttling
[ 1283.412348] nvme nvme0: iops=4300 -> 1400 (throttle)
[ 1286.512001] kubelet: attach timeout: failed to attach GPU to pod abc-123 (attach timed out)
```

sunil: which nvme fw + kernel? did we roll anything in that region recently?

alex: fw=SMX-3.4.1 (pushed 2w ago to ap-southeast), kernel=6.4.1. Only ap-southeast got that FW change during the last maintenance window.

ben: @sunil @rachel i'm looking. Can we get a quick list of hot nodes? alex, run the nvme temp scan script and paste node ids.

alex: ran `scripts/list-hot-nodes --region ap-southeast1 --metric nvme_temp_grad --threshold 15` -> 15 hosts flagged, 3 hosts already returned gpu-attach errors. Pasted IDs to the devops board.

rachel: confirmed — most anomalies concentrated in ap-southeast1-b. Not global.

sunil: short-term mitigation: 1) taint flagged nodes with `taint/ephemeral-nvme-hot:NoSchedule` 2) throttle node-provisioner concurrency for that region to 1 attach per host 3) reduce batch allocation for pending GPU jobs. I can push a config change now.

alex: applying taint now and reducing concurrency for node-provisioner. Taint command:
```
kubectl taint nodes gnode-ase1-0{42..56} ephemeral-nvme-hot=true:NoSchedule
```

deploy-bot: [deploy] config: node-provisioner v2.6.1 -> v2.6.2 - concurrency cap for ap-southeast1 set to 1. Rollout started.

ben: open ticket with vendor (Samsung-XX NVMe series) for thermal calibration and FW correlation. Also collect `nvme-cli` smart logs and vendor debug dump. Alex, upload `nvme-cli --admin-get-log` outputs to /artifacts/nvme-dumps/3311223344.tar.gz.

alex: uploading tarball now, path: s3://redwood-artifacts/infra/nvme-dumps/3311223344.tar.gz. Also capturing `iostat -x 1 10` for the flagged hosts.

sunil: migration note: scheduled drain of flagged nodes and live-migration of queued gpu pods will take ~30-45m given current backlog. I'll start canary reattaches after taint & config complete.

rachel: do we want to move capacity to us-west2 temporarily? That will impact latency for some customers. Cost/latency tradeoff?

ben: for critical queues yes, move small batch to us-west2, leave non-critical on hold. I'll coordinate with capacity-planning to keep costs minimal.

alex: one more datapoint — scrub jobs overlap with peak batch window on those hosts. Disk temp gradient seems to spike after scrub start. We should avoid scheduling deep scrubs during high-provision windows.

sunil: agreed — adding scrub-avoid window to the scrub controller for ap-southeast1 between 16:00-20:00 local. Patch coming in 10m.

ben: INC-2026-3311 created. Actions: vendor ticket, taint nodes, throttle concurrency, migrate critical workloads, collect dumps, schedule maintenance if vendor recommends FW rollback. Next status update in 20m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

rachel: thanks — keep pings in this thread. If any host flips to failed state, ping @oncall immediately.

alex: noted. Avoiding FW rollback until vendor confirms correlation. Captured nvme-core logs and uploaded.

ben: thanks team. Good mitigation plan — prefer software-level mitigations (taints, concurrency, scheduling) until hardware vendor advises.

rachel: update at +20m or earlier if anything changes. :thumbsup:
